_note: Config for emit_summit_matrix.py — the SUMMIT side of estMatrix for AMZN (the model's own estimates per snapshot). The consensus side has its own map_amzn.json.
_derived_note: QUARTERLY totals are not modelled directly — the model's own quarterly REV and OP_INCOME rows are literal 0 forward (and OP_INCOME once reads 197000 for a single quarter, which is the annual frame leaking into a quarterly cell: never read it). Both totals are therefore the sum of the three segment rows, which is exactly how the dataset's hand-built quarterly `summit` column was constructed and how it ties to the reported total. ANNUAL is the opposite: REV / EBITDA / EARNINGS / CAPEX are populated directly per year, so they are read straight.
_sign_note: The model carries capex as negative cash flow; every Results dataset shows it as positive spend.
_vintages_note: All 7 Summit snapshots, distinct by facts_hash. lastActual = the last period the model had REPORTED when that file was saved — established from the data, not from the calendar: 2026-07-30 and 2026-08-03 still carry the MAY projection for 2Q26 (AWS 39,826 against a 42,232 print), so both are pre-print saves despite their dates; 2026-08-04 is the re-cut that ingested it (AWS 3Q26 41,918 -> 44,558, FY26 AWS 166,210 -> 173,476). 2026-05-13 differs from 2026-05-05 on annual EBITDA — the MCP-vs-file reconciliation flagged in RESULTS_CONVENTIONS §4 — so both are kept and the picker can show the gap rather than hiding it.
_views_note: Which dataset metric keys get a matrix row per view. Quarterly capex and EPS are absent on purpose: the model projects capex ANNUALLY only (its quarterly row is a literal 0) and carries no EPS row at all, so both would be manufactured. Annual op-income lines are absent because the dataset's annual view has no segment op-income metrics to plot them on.
_evolution_note: Feeds emit_evolution.py — the Estimates pane's own block. Same dumps, opposite read: every year on the axis, forward or already reported, because the pane plots how the model's view of a year moved. Total op income is DERIVED here (the model zeroes its own total row) while annual revenue is read straight, which is why this block carries its own `derived`. `prior` is FY2025, the year before years[0], used for the first year's implied growth on the Top Line metrics.

evolution._cons_metrics_note: The BBG figure the MODEL stores inside the same snapshot block — same save date as the solid line, which is exactly the claim this pane makes. The model carries these three only.
evolution._cons_map_note: For lines the model stores no consensus for, mapped off the Bloomberg workbook's own calendar (each model date takes the Street's latest file on or before it — up to ~3 months stale, so each affected note says so). Only possible at all since the Aug-2026 export started carrying segment revenue and capex; before that these were Summit-only. Segment OP INCOME is deliberately left out: the annual view has no metric to hang it on, and adding a matrix row purely to feed this generator would put numbers in the dataset the Results pane can never draw.

_axis_note: The dataset's period axis — cells outside it are dropped so the matrix never carries a period the metric cannot plot.
